content:
Hi, while checking some Sashiko findings in the patch series that implements #[should_panic] [1] in KUnit, I realized that implementing #[ignore] [2] attribute would be fairly easy. That said, would it be useful?

It could come in handy while developing tests or to have tests already coded that are waiting for a feature to be available (this is the case in the bitmap.rs file, waiting for #[should_panic] [3]) but I am not sure if it is enough justification to code and send a patch.

Thanks

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/rust-for-linux/20260930-rust_kunit_v4-v1-0-e3b0d45311dd@gmail.com/T/#t
[2] https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-ignore-attribute
[3] https://github.com/Rust-for-Linux/linux/blob/rust-next/rust/kernel/bitmap.rs#L767-L775
I think the main place where #[ignore] might be useful is if #[cfg_attr(CONFIG_FOO, ignore)] works
which may be more tricky to implement

If you think it would be useful I could give it a try, in the current implementation [1] the test is skipped preemptively and only run if the cfg is enabled (the patch series I sent simply removes the test from the TEST_CASES array)

A possible implementation (first thing I thought could not make sense) could be expanding #[cfg_attr(CONFIG_FOO, ignore)] to

#[cfg(CONFIG_FOO)]
{
 test.status = ignore;
}

#[cfg(not(CONFIG_FOO))]
{
test.status = success;
test();
}

in the test body

[1] https://github.com/Rust-for-Linux/linux/blob/rust-next/rust/macros/kunit.rs#L138-L151
